title: Getting to an appointment
scenario: You have an appointment tomorrow at 10:00 AM.

questions.text: What could help you get there on time?

options.text: Set an alarm and plan how you will get there.
options.feedback: Planning ahead can make it easier to arrive on time.

options.text: Wait until tomorrow morning to decide.
options.feedback: You could still make the appointment, but planning ahead gives you more time to deal with problems.

options.text: Wait until the appointment time and then decide.
options.feedback: It is usually easier to solve travel problems before the appointment time.

completionMessage: You practiced planning ahead.

title: Finding your keys
scenario: You need to leave home, but you cannot find your keys.

options.text: Search the places where you usually keep your keys.
options.feedback: Starting with places you commonly use is a practical first step.

options.text: Immediately assume someone took them.
options.feedback: That is an assumption. Checking what you can observe gives you more information.

options.text: Give up looking.
options.feedback: There may be simple places you can check first.

completionMessage: You practiced checking information before making a conclusion.

title: The bus has left
scenario: You arrive at the bus stop and your bus has already left. You have an appointment in 30 minutes.

options.text: Whether another bus or form of transport is available.
options.feedback: Looking for another practical option keeps the problem-solving process moving.

options.text: Give up immediately.
options.feedback: There may be alternatives worth checking.

options.text: Wait without checking anything.
options.feedback: Checking available options may help you decide what to do next.

completionMessage: You practiced looking for alternatives.

title: No food at home
scenario: You have no food at home and ₹200 available.

questions.text: What information could help you decide what to do?

options.text: What food you need and how much it costs.
options.feedback: Knowing your needs and prices helps you make a practical decision.

options.text: Buy the first thing you see.
options.feedback: This might work, but checking your needs and budget gives you more information.

options.text: Spend all the money without checking prices.
options.feedback: Checking prices helps avoid an unexpected problem.

completionMessage: You practiced gathering information before deciding.

title: Low phone battery
scenario: Your phone battery is at 5%. You need your phone later today.

options.text: Charge it when possible and think about when you will need it.
options.feedback: This considers both the immediate problem and what you will need later.

options.text: Ignore the battery.
options.feedback: The battery may run out before you need the phone.

options.text: Keep using it without considering the battery.
options.feedback: Thinking ahead can help prevent a later problem.

completionMessage: You practiced thinking ahead.

title: Several bills
scenario: You have several bills to pay, but you do not have enough money to pay them all today.

options.text: Check the amounts and due dates.
options.feedback: Knowing amounts and deadlines gives you information for prioritizing.

options.text: Pick one randomly.
options.feedback: Random choice does not use the information available.

options.text: Ignore all of them.
options.feedback: Ignoring bills can allow problems to grow.

completionMessage: You practiced prioritizing using information.

title: Buying something
scenario: You have ₹500. You want something that costs ₹450.

questions.text: What else should you consider before buying it?

options.text: Whether you need the item and whether you will have enough money for important expenses.
options.feedback: A good decision considers both the purchase and what you may need later.

options.text: Buy it immediately because you have enough for the item.
options.feedback: You can afford the item, but other expenses may also matter.

options.text: Do not think about money at all.
options.feedback: Considering your available money helps you make a practical choice.

completionMessage: You practiced thinking about consequences before deciding.

title: A friend asks to borrow money
scenario: A friend asks to borrow ₹1,000, but you need your money for your own expenses.

options.text: Explain that you cannot afford to lend the money.
options.feedback: It is reasonable to consider your own needs and communicate your limit.

options.text: Give them the money even though you need it.
options.feedback: Helping someone may be important, but your own essential needs matter too.

options.text: Avoid answering without saying anything.
options.feedback: A clear response can reduce confusion.

completionMessage: You practiced balancing your needs with another person's request.

title: Unexpected bill
scenario: You receive a bill that you were not expecting.

questions.text: What should you do before deciding what to do about it?

options.text: Check what the bill is for and when it is due.
options.feedback: Checking the details gives you information for the next step.

options.text: Immediately assume it is a mistake.
options.feedback: You may not have enough information to know that yet.

options.text: Ignore it.
options.feedback: Checking the bill first can help you decide what to do.

completionMessage: You practiced checking facts before deciding.

title: Overspending
scenario: You planned to spend ₹1,000 this week but spent ₹1,400.

options.text: Look at where the extra ₹400 was spent and make a plan.
options.feedback: Reviewing what happened can help you make a more useful plan.

options.text: Decide that budgeting does not work.
options.feedback: One difficult week does not tell you whether every plan will work.

options.text: Ignore what happened.
options.feedback: Reviewing what happened gives you information for next time.

completionMessage: You practiced learning from what happened.

title: No reply
scenario: You sent a message to a friend yesterday. They have not replied.

options.text: There could be several reasons they have not replied.
options.feedback: There may be several explanations, and you do not have enough information to know which one is true.

options.text: They definitely do not want to talk to me.
options.feedback: That is one possible interpretation, but the available information does not prove it.

options.text: They are definitely angry with me.
options.feedback: You do not have enough information to know how they feel.

completionMessage: You practiced separating facts from assumptions.

title: Cancelled plans
scenario: A friend cancels your plans for tomorrow.

options.text: Ask whether you could arrange another time.
options.feedback: Looking for another possibility keeps the situation flexible.

options.text: Assume the friendship is over.
options.feedback: One cancelled plan does not provide enough information for that conclusion.

options.text: Never speak to them again.
options.feedback: There may be other explanations and options.

completionMessage: You practiced considering more than one possible response.

title: Neighbour complaint
scenario: Your neighbour says that you were making too much noise.

options.text: Ask what happened and what time the noise was a problem.
options.feedback: Getting more information can help you understand the situation.

options.text: Immediately argue with them.
options.feedback: Responding before understanding the problem may make it harder to resolve.

options.text: Assume they are trying to cause trouble.
options.feedback: That is an assumption that may not be supported by the information you have.

completionMessage: You practiced gathering information before responding.

title: Misunderstanding
scenario: Someone says they misunderstood something you told them.

options.text: Ask what they understood and explain what you meant.
options.feedback: Checking what the other person understood can help identify the problem.

options.text: Assume they are deliberately misunderstanding you.
options.feedback: You may not know their reason without more information.

options.text: Stop communicating.
options.feedback: Clarifying the misunderstanding may be a useful option.

completionMessage: You practiced clarifying a misunderstanding.

title: Unclear work instruction
scenario: Someone at work asks you to complete a task, but you do not understand what they want.

questions.text: What is a useful next step?

options.text: Ask them to explain the task or show you an example.
options.feedback: Asking for clarification can prevent mistakes and help you learn the task.

options.text: Pretend you understand.
options.feedback: Pretending may lead to avoidable mistakes.

options.text: Do something completely different.
options.feedback: Getting clarification first gives you better information.

completionMessage: You practiced asking for clarification.

title: Running late
scenario: You are getting ready for an appointment and realize you are running late.

options.text: How long it will take to get there and whether you should contact the person you are meeting.
options.feedback: This considers the remaining time and a practical communication step.

options.text: Ignore the time.
options.feedback: The remaining time matters when deciding what to do.

options.text: Cancel immediately without checking your options.
options.feedback: Cancellation may be an option in some situations, but checking what is still possible first may help.

completionMessage: You practiced adjusting a plan when circumstances change.

title: Two tasks
scenario: Two tasks need to be completed today. One is due at 12 PM. The other is due at 6 PM.

questions.text: Which should you consider doing first?

options.text: The task due at 12 PM.
options.feedback: The earlier deadline is an important factor when prioritizing.

options.text: Whichever task looks easiest.
options.feedback: Ease can matter, but the deadline is also important.

options.text: Choose randomly.
options.feedback: Using available information is more useful than choosing randomly.

completionMessage: You practiced prioritizing tasks.

title: Mistake at work
scenario: You notice that you made a mistake at work.

options.text: Check what happened and tell the appropriate person if necessary.
options.feedback: Understanding the mistake and taking an appropriate corrective step can help resolve it.

options.text: Hide the mistake.
options.feedback: Hiding a problem can make it harder to correct.

options.text: Pretend nothing happened.
options.feedback: Recognizing a problem gives you a chance to address it.

completionMessage: You practiced recognizing and addressing a problem.

title: Do not know how
scenario: You have been asked to complete something you do not know how to do.

options.text: Ask someone appropriate for guidance.
options.feedback: Getting guidance is a practical way to learn what to do.

options.text: Pretend you know how.
options.feedback: Pretending can lead to avoidable mistakes.

options.text: Give up immediately.
options.feedback: There may be support or information available.

completionMessage: You practiced help-seeking.

title: Solution did not work
scenario: You tried something to solve a problem, but it did not work.

options.text: Think about what happened and consider another approach.
options.feedback: Reviewing what happened can help you choose a different approach.

options.text: Decide that nothing can be done.
options.feedback: One unsuccessful attempt does not prove that no solution exists.

options.text: Keep doing exactly the same thing without considering why it did not work.
options.feedback: Trying again can sometimes help, but considering what happened may reveal a better approach.

completionMessage: You practiced reflection and flexible thinking.
